findings.defect: “Bother” weakens a question about whether the giant physically attacked or laid hands on anyone else.
findings.rationale: Taekyung is specifically worried about the physical safety of Hwangbo Ak’s companions, as confirmed by his subsequent question about whether the giant fought them.
findings.replacement: “Did you lay a hand on anyone else?”

findings.current: But gently soothing him like a kindergartner was enough.
findings.defect: The draft omits the comic specificity of treating him like a kindergartner from the “Sunshine Class.”
findings.rationale: 햇님 반 is an intentionally childish kindergarten class name that sharpens the contrast between the giant’s physique and behavior.
findings.replacement: But gently coaxing him like a kindergartner from the Sunshine Class was enough.
findings.source: 사마외도라길래 그냥 때려눕혀야 하나, 생각했는데 햇님 반 유치원생 대하듯이 살살 달래 주는 것으로도 충분했다.

findings.current: This was my first time meeting him, but Hwangbo Ak and the giant apparently knew each other.
findings.defect: The draft invents a prior acquaintance between Hwangbo Ak and the giant. The source contrasts Taekyung not knowing Hwangbo Ak with Hwangbo Ak apparently recognizing Taekyung.
findings.rationale: Hwangbo Ak has just addressed Taekyung by his sobriquet; nothing in the source says that Hwangbo Ak and the giant previously knew each other.
findings.replacement: He was a stranger to me, but apparently I wasn’t to him.

findings.current: We’re all members of the Murim Alliance.
findings.defect: The draft omits the claim that everyone in the Murim Alliance is “one family,” leaving Hwangbo Ak’s immediate objection about being one family without a clear antecedent.
findings.rationale: 한 식구 explicitly supplies both Taekyung’s conciliatory claim and the wording that Hwangbo Ak challenges in the next line.
findings.replacement: We’re all one family in the Murim Alliance.

findings.current: Materials, dust, and dirt scattered across the ground were blasted more than three zhang away, and the people nearby sucked in startled breaths.
findings.defect: The draft changes the stated result from debris being pushed outside a three-zhang radius to each item traveling more than three zhang.
findings.rationale: 반경 삼 장 밖으로 describes the boundary beyond which the debris is driven, not the distance traveled by every object.
findings.replacement: Materials, dust, and dirt scattered across the ground were blasted beyond a three-zhang radius, and the people nearby sucked in startled breaths.
findings.source: 땅바닥에 널브러져 있던 자재와 먼지, 흙 따위가 반경 삼 장 밖으로 밀려나고 사람들이 헛숨을 삼켰다.

findings.current: If I had left him alone, I would have stripped him down to his soul.
findings.defect: The draft makes Taekyung the hypothetical attacker. The source says Hwangbo Ak would have been utterly thrashed if Taekyung had allowed the fight to continue.
findings.rationale: 털렸을 marks Hwangbo Ak as the recipient of the hypothetical beating; Taekyung’s role was preventing that outcome.
findings.replacement: If I’d let the fight continue, he would’ve had his soul beaten out of him.
findings.source: 계속 놔뒀으면 영혼까지 탈탈 털렸을 놈이다.

findings.current: “Don’t stretch your legs until you’ve checked where you’re lying down.”
findings.defect: The literal calque is opaque and unnatural in English, obscuring the warning to assess whom one is challenging.
findings.rationale: The Korean proverb warns someone to judge the situation and their own position before acting; Taekyung applies it specifically to Hwangbo Ak choosing dangerous opponents.
findings.replacement: “Know who you’re dealing with before you pick a fight.”

summary: Two critical subject/relationship errors, two major fidelity defects, and three localized omissions or wording issues.
